## User stage forcings: TorchScript modules called every stage (`set_user_stage_forcings`) {#sec-ch09-user}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Calls user TorchScript modules once per Runge–Kutta stage and adds what they return to the
hydro and scalar increments.
**Switch.** The C++ or Python call `MeshBlockImpl::set_user_stage_forcings(filenames)`; there is no YAML key.
Default: none.
**Requires.** Each module returns `Dict[str, Tensor]` with keys `hydro_du` and/or `scalar_ds` of the increments'
shapes; `scalar_ds` needs passive scalars.
**Order.** As the user writes it; the returned value is an increment over the full step.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch09-user-add.
:::

A user stage forcing is a source term written in Python, compiled with `torch.jit.script`, saved, and loaded by
file name. In every stage the block hands each module one dictionary with all its buffers and the stage variables,
the step $\Delta t$ and the stage index, and adds what the module returns to the native increments, after the
native forcings, the vertical implicit correction and the passive-scalar update, and before the Runge–Kutta
average. A user dry-air density change carries the passive tracers like a native one.

The returned `hydro_du` is added as it is. The framework does not multiply it by $\Delta t$: a module that models
a rate $\mathbf S$ returns $\Delta t\,\mathbf S$ itself.

### Derivation

Let $\Delta\mathbf U^{\mathrm{nat}}$ be the native increment of the stage (@eq-ch09-framework-stage plus the
implicit correction) and $\mathbf G^{q}$ the `hydro_du` of user module $q = 1..Q$. The stage hands the
integrator

$$
\Delta\mathbf U = \Delta\mathbf U^{\mathrm{nat}} + \sum_{q=1}^{Q}\mathbf G^{q}(\mathbf V, \Delta t, s),
$$ {#eq-ch09-user-add}

with $\mathbf V$ the dictionary of block buffers and stage variables. @eq-ch09-user-add is applied to the `user_stage_forcings` in
[`meshblock.cpp:689-742`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L689-L742). Each module sees $\mathbf V$ as it was before any user module ran, because the dictionary is built once by `stage_forcing_variables`
([`meshblock.cpp:731-738`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L731-L738)). Through the Runge–Kutta average a user
increment enters the step with the stage weight $w_2^{(s)}$, exactly as a native one; the test below asserts that
for rk1, rk2, rk3 and rk3s4. No closed form is involved, so no executable check is attached.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-user-forcing shows the interface. The modules are moved to the block's device when they are loaded by `set_user_stage_forcings`
([`meshblock.cpp:96-109`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L96-L109)) and are called on that device. They run once per stage of every step, and
again in a redone step (Chapter 7).

: Code map of the user stage forcings. {#tbl-ch09-user-code}

1. `set_user_stage_forcings` loads every file with `torch::jit::load`, moves it to the block's device and puts it in evaluation mode, in
   `set_user_stage_forcings` ([`meshblock.cpp:96-109`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L96-L109)).
2. In `advance_local`, after the native and scalar tendencies, the block builds the dictionary with
   `stage_forcing_variables` ([`meshblock.cpp:38-48`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L38-L48)): every named buffer first, then the stage variables,
   which replace a buffer of the same name.
3. It calls each of the `user_stage_forcings` with the dictionary, $\Delta t$ and the stage index
   ([`meshblock.cpp:731-738`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L731-L738)), checks the result with
   `stage_forcing_result` ([`meshblock.cpp:50-65`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L50-L65)) and adds it in `apply_extra_forcing`
   ([`meshblock.cpp:690-723`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L690-L723)), which refuses a wrong shape, an unknown key, or `scalar_ds` without
   scalars.
4. The user dry-density change carries the tracers with `carry_dry_source`
   ([`meshblock.cpp:740-742`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L740-L742)), against the scalar increment from before the user modules, so an
   explicit `scalar_ds` is not debited by a simultaneous dry removal.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_jit_user_forcing.py` (`test_jit_user_forcing_python`) | a scripted module with a nested submodule and a buffer adds $0.25\cdot1 + 0.5$ to the dry density in one stage at $\Delta t = 0$ | `torch.testing.assert_close` defaults (float64: rtol $10^{-7}$, atol $10^{-7}$) | the returned value is added as is, not times $\Delta t$ |
| `tests/test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer.py` (`test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer_python`) | for rk1, rk2, rk3, rk3s4 a user dry increment in stage $s$ changes the density by $w_2^{(s)}$ times it; an explicit `scalar_ds` is not coupled to a dry removal; tracer ratios stay in $[-10^{-12}, 1+10^{-12}]$ | $10^{-12}$ absolute | round-off of a few operations on values of order 1 |

: Tests of the user stage forcings. {#tbl-ch09-user-tests}

**Evidence.** No number is quoted. **Pending: pinned ctest run** of both tests at the pin.
**Coverage.** CPU in CI. `test_stage_forcing_dry_tracer.py` takes `--device cuda`; whether a CUDA arm is
registered at the pin is not checked here. No multi-rank arm.

### Limits

1. **No time scaling.** A module that returns a rate instead of $\Delta t$ times the rate is wrong by a factor
   $\Delta t$, with no warning.
2. **Through the limited EOS.** A module whose increment drives the state through a floor makes the step redo
   (chengcli/snapy#226); the redo machinery is Chapter 7 and Chapter 8.
3. **Ordering.** User modules see the stage variables, not the native increment; a module cannot react to what the
   native forcings did in the same stage.
